_about: Fact check of 1 Nov 2026 (scheduled): the 257 facts first scheduled for 26 Nov-25 Dec 2026 and not yet in the ledger. WebSearch only (titles, mostly no snippets) plus the checkers’ own knowledge; 61 facts ran out of the first run’s search budget and were re-checked with searches. Restamping then brought in 4 more facts (sport:14, animals:37, animals:24, places:1), checked the same way. Applied with tools/apply-ballpark-fixes.js.

animals:10.q: How wide can a wandering albatross’s wings be, tip to tip, in metres?

animals:24.q: How tall can an emperor penguin grow, in centimetres?
animals:24.n: Up to about 115 cm, the height of a six-year-old child.

animals:41.n: It eats, drinks and is thought to sleep on the wing.

animals:86.q: How many days can a male emperor penguin go without food during the breeding season?
animals:86.n: Courting, then guarding the egg through the Antarctic winter, losing almost half his weight.

body:20.q: How many bones make up the human skull, not counting the ear bones?

body:38.q: How many vertebrae are in the human neck?
body:38.n: 7, the same number as a giraffe’s.

science:66.q: What is the highest voltage carried by Britain’s National Grid power lines, in volts?
